title: Rapid Sparring Brief — Inference Countermoves
content:
Purpose:
A compact, field-ready sparring brief for AEs and SEs to use when facing LLM API competitors. Focus: concise counters framed around three buying axes (economics, reliability, deployability). This is intentionally tactical — snippets for calls, demo flows, and escalation triggers.

Audience & use cases:
- AE + SE pre-call prep (3–5 min read)
- Deal coaching in SDR/AE sparring sessions
- Quick reference in playbooks or on-call Slack channel during live demos

Core positioning pillars (one-liners):
1) Predictable economics: "We optimize for unit cost at production scale — not just list price per token."
2) Production-grade reliability: "Fallbacks, routing, and SLA-backed reserved capacity keep customer apps live during spikes and incidents."
3) Unified ops across modes: "Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private = same API, same monitoring, same QA surface."

Common competitor themes and tight counters (short):
- Competitor: "Cheaper per-token on the public API."
  Counter: "Per-token discounts are noise if requests queue or you overprovision GPUs. We cut unit cost via batching, prefix/KV caching, and model routing. Customer examples: 30% lower steady-state token cost after optimizing batching + caching."

- Competitor: "We have more models and bigger model catalog."
  Counter: "Catalog size ≠ production quality. We validate model throughput, latency profiles, and failure modes, and publish verified profiles so you can pick model variants that meet SLOs. Documentation + sample SLOs reduce integration risk."

- Competitor: "We give full model access for on-prem; you lock into us."
  Counter: "Our Private option supports air-gapped & VPC installs while preserving portability — same interface and rollout policies so migration risk is minimal. We treat portability as a first-class constraint."

Objection ladder: from surface objections -> escalation scripts
- O1 (price objection): "Their per-token is lower, why pay more?"
  Script: "Totally fair — can I ask a couple quick questions about your traffic shape and latency needs? Often per-token wins evaporate once you hit production throughput and need burst capacity or predictable latency. We can run a short TCO sketch with your qps profile in 48 hours."

- O2 (feature parity): "They have feature X (tool-calling/structured output)."
  Script: "Great — which parts of X matter for your product? Our SDKs support streaming + structured output and we have built-in tests and monitored regressions tied to evals to ensure those features stay stable across model updates."

- O3 (vendor lock-in / roadmap): "We fear getting stuck with you."
  Script: "We see migration as part of the partnership. We'll provide exportable artifacts, pinned model versions, and operational runbooks during onboarding. If you need escape hatches, our dedicated team will deliver a migration plan as part of the contract."

Demo checklist (quick):
1) Start with perf narrative — show a live trace (token-level latency) on a small payload.
2) Inject a simulated spike (or show recorded trace) to show routing fallback and canary behavior.
3) Show console cost breakdown for same request across two model/quantization profiles.
4) Pull up rollouts UI and show canary -> full rollout + automatic fallback.
5) If asked about private: show diff between hosted and private network topology + KMS/HSM integration points.

Tactical rebuttal snippets to copy into chat or email (short bullets):
- "We reduce unit cost via batching/caching and route traffic to lower-cost variants when it meets your quality bar — not by sacrificing latency guarantees."
- "Reserved capacity gives you predictable spikes without expensive overprovisioning."
- "Audit logs + KMS integrations let you meet compliance without sacrificing developer velocity."

Red flags and escalation triggers (when to loop solutions/eng):
- Customer demands an SLA on peaky multi-region workloads >200k qps — loop infra for dedicated sizing.
- Customer insists on model variant with no production profiling data — loop Applied ML to run a quick throughput/latency validation.
- Tight procurement window and termination clauses — loop legal for template concession terms.

Competitive traps (what rivals try and how to avoid falling for it):
- Trap: Competitor promises immediate migration support but provides no runbooks or validated performance docs.
  How to avoid: Ask for a short checklist: runbooks, model profiling data, performance playbook. If missing, emphasize migration risk and quantify timelines.

- Trap: Overemphasis on headline model size (bigger model = better).
  How to avoid: Reframe to SLOs and unit economics. Ask for latency/throughput numbers for target sequence lengths.

Metrics to put in the contract conversation (show, don’t tell):
- p95 token latency (real workload)
- average tokens per request and batching efficiency
- KV cache hit rate (if using prefix caching)
- Cost per 1M effective tokens after batching/caching (TCO sketch)

Persona playbooks (one-liners to use):
- CTO/Reliability lead: "Show me p95 traces, fallback policies, and on-call runbooks." Lead with reliability pillars and SLA terms.
- Head of ML/Infra: "Show model throughput profiles, quantization implications, and kernel-level optimizations." Have Applied ML notes ready.
- Product manager: "How does this affect feature velocity and edge cases?" Focus on SDKs, evals, and rollout safety nets.

Open items / next 48h deliverables (for GTM ops):
- Draft a 1‑page TCO sketch template for AE use (owner: Marcus) — due 2025-11-07.
- Update demo lab to include a canned spike recording for show-and-tell (owner: Sophie) — due 2025-11-10.
- Add two new rebuttal snippets to the shared Slack snippet library (owner: Darren) — due 2025-11-05.

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep this doc concise — field wants <1 page cheat.
- Ask Applied ML for one high-level customer story: "we cut tokens cost by 27% after batching and enabling KV cache" with before/after numbers.
- Cross-link to technical deep-dive for SEs (Confluence page).

Quick reference — 30s elevator script for SDR handoff:
"Redwood helps teams ship LLM features with predictable performance and lower real-world unit costs. We give you the same API across hosted, dedicated, and private modes so you can scale without reengineering — and we back it with tooling (rollouts, tracing, cost maps) so you don’t get surprised at scale."
